label: Plan 2
description: Produce an execution-ready plan with canonical issue acceptance criteria, evidence-backed Clean Architecture/SOLID analysis, explicit ADR conformance, and independently verifiable phases. Plans only — no implementation. If you decide to use sub agents, always set openai-oauth/gpt-5.5 · effort: low.
when_to_use: Use experimentally when planning already-agreed work and evaluating stronger issue-readiness, architecture, ADR, and conformance preparation. Do NOT use to decide WHAT to build or to implement changes.

guards.message: This workflow produces a plan, not implementation. Complete all planning and review gates before delivering it; never merge.

steps.label: Establish and verify the independent planning baseline
steps.guidance: Before drafting acceptance criteria or a plan, spawn a read-only investigator with only the original issue, its comments/references, and repository access; do not show it any draft, proposed solution, or prior planning artifact. It must independently produce a cited baseline containing: source outcomes and constraints; valid resolution space; examples distinguished from requirements; explicit non-goals; verified current-state facts; applicable architecture/ADR constraints; unresolved human decisions; and the most concrete reproducible evidence appropriate to the work (tests/commands when known, otherwise named scenarios, observable measurements, inspections, artifacts, or approvals). Then spawn a fresh read-only verifier, still without any draft plan, to challenge source fidelity, evidence, omissions, and speculative options. Resolve findings and freeze the result as `PLANNING BASELINE v1` with a content hash or stable artifact location. Missing source/evidence is a blocker, never a PASS. Later changes require a versioned amendment with cited new evidence or an explicit recorded human decision plus fresh independent verification. Done when `INDEPENDENT BASELINE: PASS` is evidence-backed and frozen before drafting begins.

steps.label: Ground the plan in the issue and code
steps.guidance: Resolve the linked issue and read its body, comments, referenced product/design documents, the frozen `PLANNING BASELINE`, and its evidence. Verify the baseline artifact/hash and record any disagreement; do not silently reinterpret it. Use it to ground the intended outcome, constraints, non-goals, valid resolution space, unresolved requirements, and verified starting state. If new evidence or an explicit human decision changes the baseline, create a versioned amendment and independently verify it before continuing. If a product decision is missing, stop and identify it rather than inventing a requirement. Done when planning inputs match the current verified baseline.

steps.label: Prepare canonical acceptance criteria and non-goals
steps.guidance: Draft stable identifiers and GitHub checkboxes for independently checkable behavioural acceptance criteria: `- [ ] **AC1:** ...`. Derive them from the frozen `PLANNING BASELINE`; include applicable positive, negative, boundary, failure, compatibility, documentary, operational, and protocol outcomes without prescribing implementation. Draft explicit out-of-scope/non-goals. Keep issue AC boxes unchecked. Preserve every baseline-valid resolution unless verified new evidence or an explicit recorded human decision eliminates it; never turn an example into a requirement. Classify every unresolved choice as exactly one of: a human/product blocker; bounded implementation discovery with objective selection criteria; or speculative/invalid and removed. An unproven interpretation must not become an executable phase. Done when `ISSUE READINESS: PASS` is supportable and every criterion and unresolved choice is unambiguous.

steps.label: Analyze Clean Architecture and SOLID impact
steps.guidance: Inspect affected code paths, architecture tests, ports, adapters, shared mechanisms, and external consumers. Produce cited analysis of affected layers, responsibility ownership, dependency direction, existing mechanisms to reuse, public API impact, and abstraction altitude. Evaluate SOLID only where concretely applicable: mixed responsibilities, extension points, substitutability, interface width, and dependency inversion; explicitly mark irrelevant principles rather than inventing abstractions. Identify forbidden test-only production paths and speculative surface. Done when the intended ownership and dependency direction are explicit and evidence-backed.

steps.label: Inventory ADRs and establish conformance
steps.guidance: Search the repository ADR directory/index, affected documentation and code references, and issue/PR references. Build a table of each relevant ADR, status, relevance, and how the plan complies. Record the search locations even when no ADR applies. An apparent conflict with an accepted ADR blocks delivery unless the plan includes the repository's process to amend or supersede it. Decide whether the work creates a durable architectural decision requiring a new ADR; do not propose one for a local implementation detail. Done when `ADR CONFORMANCE: PASS` is supportable or the conflict is escalated.

steps.label: Map every acceptance criterion to verification
steps.guidance: Create an AC-to-plan-to-verification matrix with stable AC id, planned phase, evidence method, level, and required falsifiability/parity/observation/inspection/approval artifact. Every AC needs reproducible evidence appropriate to the issue type, at the most concrete level currently knowable: exact existing commands/tests when verified; otherwise named scenarios or tests to add, measurable operational observations, documentary inspection criteria, or explicit decision artifacts and approvers. Never invent commands. Every planned check must trace to an AC, cited regression risk, or named invariant. A requirement discovered here returns through a verified baseline amendment and issue readiness. Done when no AC is unmapped.

steps.label: Draft independently verifiable phases
steps.guidance: Draft a top-level `## Execution Checklist` with one checkbox per phase, followed by one section per phase. Each phase must state its deliverable, AC ids covered, architectural owner/layer, relevant ADR constraints, expected mechanisms or indicative files, verification commands/evidence, concrete `### Task checklist`, and green-tree exit condition. Order phases by dependency; each must be independently verifiable and leave the tree green. Preserve shape-specific discipline such as feature RED/GREEN, bug reproduction, or refactor characterization/mutation/parity. Include non-goals and open questions. Done when an executor can begin phase 1 without inventing architecture, requirements, or verification.

steps.label: Review acceptance criteria and testability
steps.guidance: Spawn a read-only reviewer focused only on requirement quality and testability. Check that ACs are behavioural, independently checkable, complete across relevant boundaries and failures, free of hidden implementation prescriptions, and all mapped to planned evidence; check that non-goals make scope conformance possible. Require concrete evidence and stable finding IDs. Maintain a finding ledger: accept and revise, decline with cited evidence, or mark invalid with rationale. After revisions, spawn a fresh read-only verifier for every accepted or disputed material finding; repeat review, revision, and fresh verification until no confirmed high- or medium-severity finding remains. Any later material AC or verification change invalidates this PASS and requires rerunning this lens. Done when `ISSUE READINESS: PASS` has a closed finding ledger and no surviving material finding. Use the frozen `PLANNING BASELINE` as the shared reference. A finding is not closed by textual accommodation: a fresh verifier must confirm the underlying risk is eliminated and no new ambiguity, speculative option, or scope branch was introduced.

steps.label: Review Clean Architecture and SOLID adherence
steps.guidance: Spawn a read-only architecture reviewer. Check responsibility ownership, layer boundaries, dependency direction, runtime I/O placement, port/interface width, public API necessity, reuse altitude, caller-side workarounds, test-only production paths, speculative abstractions, and every intermediate phase. Require concrete evidence and stable finding IDs. Maintain a finding ledger: accept and revise, decline with cited evidence, or mark invalid with rationale. After revisions, spawn a fresh read-only verifier for every accepted or disputed material finding; repeat until no confirmed high- or medium-severity finding remains. Any later material architecture change invalidates this PASS and requires rerunning this lens. Reject ceremonial SOLID preferences without concrete impact. Done when `ARCHITECTURE/SOLID: PASS` has cited evidence, a closed ledger, and no surviving material finding. Use the frozen `PLANNING BASELINE` as the shared reference. A finding is not closed by textual accommodation: a fresh verifier must confirm the underlying risk is eliminated and no new ambiguity, speculative option, or scope branch was introduced.

steps.label: Review ADR coverage and conformance
steps.guidance: Spawn a read-only ADR reviewer. Verify that the ADR search was adequate, all relevant accepted decisions were found, compliance claims match their actual text and status, conflicts are surfaced, and a new ADR is proposed only for a genuine durable decision. Require stable finding IDs and concrete evidence. Maintain a finding ledger: accept and revise, decline with cited evidence, or mark invalid with rationale. After revisions, spawn a fresh read-only verifier for every accepted or disputed material finding; repeat until no confirmed high- or medium-severity finding remains. Any later material decision or ADR change invalidates this PASS and requires rerunning this lens. Done when `ADR CONFORMANCE: PASS` has a closed ledger and no surviving material finding. Use the frozen `PLANNING BASELINE` as the shared reference. A finding is not closed by textual accommodation: a fresh verifier must confirm the underlying risk is eliminated and no new ambiguity, speculative option, or scope branch was introduced.

steps.label: Review sequencing, scope, and simplicity
steps.guidance: Spawn a read-only reviewer focused on code-citation accuracy, dependency ordering, independently green phases, implementation-template classification, YAGNI, regression risks, scope adherence, and AC-to-phase-to-verification traceability. Require stable finding IDs and a concrete consequence for every finding. Maintain a finding ledger: accept and revise, decline with cited evidence, or mark invalid with rationale. After revisions, spawn a fresh read-only verifier for every accepted or disputed material finding; repeat until no confirmed high- or medium-severity finding remains. Any later material sequencing or scope change invalidates this PASS and requires rerunning this lens. Done when the plan is executable, minimally scoped, fully traceable, and the ledger is closed. Use the frozen `PLANNING BASELINE` as the shared reference. A finding is not closed by textual accommodation: a fresh verifier must confirm the underlying risk is eliminated and no new ambiguity, speculative option, or scope branch was introduced.

steps.label: Verify fidelity to the source issue
steps.guidance: Spawn a fresh read-only verifier that did not draft the plan. Give it the frozen `PLANNING BASELINE`, original sources, final ACs/non-goals, and plan. Compare the delivered interpretation against the baseline and original evidence. Confirm every valid resolution remains available unless a verified baseline amendment eliminated it; no example became mandatory; no requirement was dropped, invented, or narrowed; every unresolved choice has the correct blocker/discovery/remove classification; and every AC has appropriate reproducible evidence. Findings close only when a fresh verifier confirms the underlying risk was eliminated—not merely documented or reworded—and no new ambiguity or execution branch was introduced. Material corrections require affected specialist lenses to rerun. Done when `SOURCE CONFORMANCE: PASS` has a closed ledger and no high/medium finding.

steps.label: Run two clean holistic validation rounds
steps.guidance: Freeze the candidate issue-body patch and plan. Run two fresh read-only holistic verifiers consecutively. Each receives original sources, repository evidence, and frozen `PLANNING BASELINE`; it must challenge rather than merely accept the plan's framing, compare every claim/option to the baseline, and try to disprove execution readiness across source fidelity, AC completeness, traceability, architecture/ADR conformance, independently green sequencing, issue-appropriate evidence, scope, decisions, citations, and consistency. A documented ambiguity is not resolved: every unresolved choice must be a named human blocker or bounded discovery with objective selection/stop criteria; speculative options must be removed. Close findings only when a fresh verifier confirms risk elimination and no replacement ambiguity/scope branch. Resolve material findings, rerun affected lenses, and reset the clean count after any material edit. Require two consecutive rounds with no high/medium findings. Missing inputs or PASS-by-absence is forbidden. Done when `HOLISTIC VALIDATION: PASS (2/2)` is evidence-backed against the same baseline version.

steps.label: Update the issue and attach the approved plan
steps.guidance: First confirm all three gates: `ISSUE READINESS: PASS`, `ARCHITECTURE/SOLID: PASS`, and `ADR CONFORMANCE: PASS`. Preserve unrelated issue-body content while updating its canonical Acceptance Criteria section to the approved stable unchecked checkbox ACs and its Out of scope/Non-goals section to the approved boundary. Then post the detailed plan as an issue comment and add its permalink to the issue body when practical. The issue body is canonical for requirements; the comment is canonical for execution detail. Never check AC boxes merely because planning finished. If running an experiment or dry run, do not mutate GitHub: emit the proposed issue-body patch and plan comment as artifacts instead. Done when the approved requirements and plan have stable locations, or dry-run artifacts are reported.

steps.label: Verify the delivered GitHub artifacts
steps.guidance: Re-read the actual GitHub issue body and plan comment by their returned URLs. Verify that both URLs exist and are canonical; the posted ACs/non-goals exactly match the twice-validated artifact; AC boxes remain unchecked; the posted plan is complete and unchanged; unrelated issue content is preserved; the source issue and other runs were not mutated; and no fabricated URL, placeholder, or missing artifact is reported as success. In dry-run mode, re-read the emitted files/artifacts and apply the same equality checks without claiming GitHub delivery. Any mismatch reopens delivery and all validation lenses affected by the change. Done when `DELIVERY VERIFICATION: PASS` cites the verified URLs or artifact hashes.

steps.label: Record deferred work without scope expansion
steps.guidance: Review deferred, declined, discovered-out-of-scope, and open items. In normal mode, file a follow-up issue only when it is concrete and independently actionable; otherwise record the explicit reason no issue is warranted. In experiment or dry-run mode, do not create GitHub issues: return proposed follow-up issue payloads as artifacts. Done when nothing actionable is silently dropped and the current plan has not expanded.

steps.label: Report gates and hand off
steps.guidance: Report the baseline version/hash, issue and plan locations (or dry-run artifacts), phase count, AC count, architecture ownership, relevant ADRs, the three gate verdicts, key decisions, and unresolved human questions. Recommend the correct implementation template for every phase (`feature`, `bugfix`, `refactor`, `remove`, or `chore`). Terminate straggler subagents. Done when the executor has a concise handoff and no repository implementation was performed.
